output.sql:
WITH c2024 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE is_revenue
    AND order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
    AND order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
),
c2025 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE is_revenue
    AND order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  COUNT(c2024.customer_id) AS customers_completed_2024,
  COUNT(c2025.customer_id) AS customers_also_completed_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(c2025.customer_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(c2024.customer_id), 0), 2) AS pct_also_completed_2025
FROM c2024
LEFT JOIN c2025 ON c2025.customer_id = c2024.customer_id;
output.explanation: Counts distinct customers with at least one completed (is_revenue = true) order in 2024, then checks which of them also have a completed order in 2025. The percentage is those customers divided by the 2024 customers, rounded to 2 decimals. Uses fct_orders only, so no personal data is touched.
